newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Fed Farmers says higher inflation range okay.
newsitem.headline: NZ Fed Farmers says higher inflation range okay.

text.p: Farmers would probably be able to stand the coalition government's extended inflation range of 0-3 percent as long as it was firmly applied, Federated Farmers president Malcolm Bailey said on Tuesday.
"You could argue that we have had inflation around 2.6 percent in recent times so provided the 0 to 3 range is pretty firm, it might not be too bad," NZPA reported Bailey as saying.
"We must have low inflation from the export sector point of view, but equally we don't want the dollar to climb that high and get so overvalued that the export sector is getting screwed," he said.
"It's a matter of getting the right balance and seeing how it pans out."
The target band has been raised from 0-2 percent.
The coalition government also deferred tax cuts for a year and although Federated Farmers was in favour of the cuts, their deferral was not serious, Bailey said.

"We made a strong call to all the political parties that we wanted restraint in government spending. Under the environment we have had, any increase would have been inflationary. We have been suffering the Reserve Bank's actions to maintain low inflation, so it (tax-cuts deferral) might be the lesser of two evils.

"Philosophically we would like to see the tax cuts back on track, but keeping the export sector alive is more important in the short term and if a farmer is running at a loss, getting a tax cut is irrelevant."
Bailey said Federated Farmers was relaxed about either choice on coalition partner NZ First would have made.
"At election time, New Zealanders went more to the right of the spectrum than the left, so I guess the coalition reflects that.
"Our attitude is that we work with whoever is in government -- we don't pick sides. The difference between Labour and National and their coalition partner was not great."
